state_background_check.value: Virginia's own candidacy-qualification statute (Va. Code §24.2-500) ties eligibility to run for office to eligibility to vote, and a felony conviction strips voter/candidacy qualification until civil rights are restored by the Governor — but the statute's own text limits that rule to 'any office of the Commonwealth, or of its governmental units,' i.e., Virginia state and local offices. It does not by its own text reach candidacy for the U.S. House or Senate, which are federal offices created by the U.S. Constitution, not Commonwealth offices. Under U.S. Term Limits v. Thornton, states cannot add qualifications for Congress beyond the Constitution's own age/citizenship/residency requirements anyway, so even if Virginia intended the statute to reach Congress, it could not enforce that as a matter of federal constitutional law. Net effect: a convicted felon's eligibility to run for Virginia's congressional seats is governed by the U.S. Constitution alone, not by this state statute — genuine legal certainty here, not ambiguity, but worth stating precisely because the statute's plain text could be misread as broader than it is.
state_background_check.snippet: In order to qualify as a candidate for any office of the Commonwealth, or of its governmental units, a person must be qualified to vote for and hold that office.

platform.value: The United States is the assertion that We The People are the basis of all authority; that we have the ability, indeed the mandate, to govern ourselves (Democracy); and that the rules we develop while at our best will apply equally and at all times, especially when we are at our worst (the Rule of Law).
platform.snippet: The United States of America is more than just a place; it is an Idea —the best Idea humanity has ever had. It is the assertion that We The People are the basis of all authority; that we have the ability, indeed the mandate, to govern ourselves (Democracy); and that—yes—we are all flawed, and sometimes selfish, power-hungry, factionalist, and forgetful of history; and so the rules we develop while at our best will apply equally and at all times, especially when we are at our worst (the Rule of Law).

bio_summary.value: Like most Americans these days, we here in Central and Southside Virginia have a lot on our minds. This period of unprecedented tumult, change, and uncertainty has left many of you at a loss for whom to trust, and without a sense of confidence in where we might, or even where we should, be headed as a community and nation. These are complex, foundational, and deeply personal matters that all Americans must resolve for themselves. Here, and in my candid Campaign Note video series , I offer my perspectives. Those perspectives will no doubt evolve over the coming months as I visit with you and your neighbors along the campaign trail.
